newsitem.title: INDIA: India's HPCL said seeking Exxon stake in new unit.
newsitem.headline: India's HPCL said seeking Exxon stake in new unit.

text.p: India's Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) is seeking an equity tie-up with Exxon Corp of the U.S. for a new refinery it proposes to build on the west coast, oil industry sources said.
The sources said HPCL is looking for a new partner to take the place of the Oman Oil Company, which has not taken up its 26 percent equity entitlement in the project, the sources said.
"An HPCL team is talking to Exxon," said a source, who did not wish to be identified.
HPCL officials were not immediately available for comment.

Last August, HPCL chairman H. L. Zutshi told a news conference that he had seen newspaper reports about Oman Oil's lack of interest in pursuing the project, but had no official communication to this effect.
HPCL would go ahead with the project even if Oman Oil backed out, he said.
"HPCL will go ahead with the project even if the tie-up with Oman Oil does not materialise," Zutshi said.
The refinery will have a capacity to process six million tonnes of crude a year.

M.N.Advani, managing director of Hindustan Oman Petroleum Company, had told the August news conference that land acquisition for the new refinery was proceeding smoothly at Deoghar on the western Maharashtra coast.
HPCL recently signed a memorandum of understanding with Exxon to float joint ventures to build infrastructure to store and market petroleum products in India.
